slices.brief:
Correction from the lead, which wins over anything below that differs: (1) Do not add a list that holds the five early switches (newAbout, newNews, newMembership, newClubs, myLcaRail) off in test/unit/features.test.ts or anywhere else; a test that fails the day K turns a switch on is wrong, and PHASE_0 is the one place that holds Phase 0 switches off. Keep the guard test instead: it fails only when one of those switches is on while a route its rows open is missing from src/App.tsx, which is the real hazard, and its failure message says to leave the switch off until the route exists. (2) The base of this slice is b1db093, the branch tip after slice 1's commit (1bbee50) and a merge of main that brings the Support entry into the header's More menu (fc8109d); diff against b1db093 and do not merge or rebase anything. (3) Brief 1.4's WS02 section places support as "Website help" in the footer's Contact column and the sheet's last row, so the nav model carries it there; today's header keeps its More menu with Support untouched, since newNav is off. WS02 slice 2 of 19 (ws02-02-nav-model-switches-and-signed-in-harness), the second slice of checkpoint E, on branch redesign/ws02-navigation. WS02 is the information architecture and navigation workstream: the header, the tablet and phone bars, the footer, search, the personal event strip and the My LCA menu. It is built on redesign/ws02-navigation (cut from main at 34b721c, the merge of pull request 108, WS01's checkpoint D) and merged in five checkpoints whose letters carry on from WS01's A to D: checkpoint E is slices 1 to 5, F is 6 to 8, G is 9 to 11, H is 12 to 16 and I is 17 to 19. Each checkpoint is a draft pull request against main, merged after a merge-safety review as WS01's were. Slice 1 (the record of checkpoint D's merge, brief 1.4, the 42 switches, the stale-tab reload) is committed before this slice starts, and the lead opens checkpoint E's draft pull request after it, so the pull request text this slice drafts extends that description. The base for diffs is the commit in `base` (slice 1's commit; the lead writes its hash over the placeholder b1db093 before launching). The local ref `main` is stale (4c1a466, hundreds of files away from the branch): never diff against it, and never use it to judge what this slice changed.

Main has moved since slice 1's brief was written: fc8109d (pull request 109, Thursday, October 22, 2026) puts Support back in the header's More menu, three added lines in src/components/layout/Navbar.tsx (a two-line comment and the entry `{ label: 'Support', href: '/support' }` at the end of `moreLinks`). The lead merges main into the branch after slice 1's commit, so this slice's base ALREADY CARRIES that entry. Every line number below was measured on the branch before that merge, with slice 1's work still uncommitted in the working tree, so in src/components/layout/Navbar.tsx every line after 36 sits three lines further down on the base, and REDESIGN_STATUS.md and the test files slice 1 touched may have moved by a few lines too: re-check each cited line by looking at it. Do not merge, rebase, stash, reset, check out or commit anything.

Brief 1.4 is in the tree now, at docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md (slice 1 landed it): its WS02 section is lines 568 to 733 (read it whole), its flag table is in section 0 (header row at line 212, rows 214 to 256), section 0.2 holds the rule that anything which ships with every switch off needs K's yes (Q34), and section 2.2 line 394 names src/lib/nav.ts. The decided board for labels, sections and rows is docs/redesign/decided-boards/Nav-IA-Final.dc.html (an HTML file; its text reads in order, sections A to G, and section F is the one-label table); the search design is docs/redesign/DESIGN_REPLAN_phase0.md, Q5, lines 435 to 490. What this slice is, in one view. It is groundwork every later chrome step reads, plus the way the browser tests draw a signed-in visitor. Nothing a visitor sees changes with the switches off, and nothing in src/ imports the new model yet, so the production build is expected to keep its files and sizes. In order: (1) src/lib/nav.ts (new), a pure typed model: the one source the header, the About menu, the My LCA menu, the sheet, the tabs, the footer, the trust line and search will read; (2) the chrome's one condition, which nav.ts exports: everything newNav turns on shows only when newLook is on as well; (3) one added sentence in the comments of siteSearch, eventStrip, eventStripLive and liveMarker in src/lib/features.ts; NO switch is added, because slice 1 already declared all 42 switches of 1.4's table, among them the five this slice's manifest entry gave it (newAbout, newNews, newMembership, newClubs, myLcaRail), and this slice's tests read the declared ones; (4) tests that read those switches: the five held off in test/unit/features.test.ts, and a guard in test/unit/nav.test.ts that fails when one of the five is on while a route its rows open is missing from src/App.tsx; (5) the accessibility build with the switches on (a11y-on) turns on newNav, siteSearch, eventStrip, eventStripLive and liveMarker beside newLook and themeHeritage, with every pin of that list moved; (6) a signed-in visitor for the browser tests, in test/a11y/signedIn.ts, and one persona list that both the unit tests and the browser tests read, in test/unit/fixtures/navPersonas.ts, proven by a short spec on today's header; (7) the record, a 'WS02 step 2' block in REDESIGN_STATUS.md with the rest of the WS02 section's entries; (8) a record test of its own; (9) the commit text and the pull request text, drafted. No page, style, server, migration, worker or build-config file changes, and nothing is added to package.json. With every switch off a visitor sees nothing new. Even with the a11y-on build's seven switches on, nothing reads the five that are new to it (newNav, siteSearch, eventStrip, eventStripLive and liveMarker) yet, so what that build draws does not change either. Nothing here reaches a visitor, so it needs no yes from K under Q34.

THE NAVIGATION MODEL: what brief 1.4 and the decided board say it holds (sources: WS02 section lines 585 to 593 and 676 of docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md, Nav-IA-Final sections A to G, DESIGN_REPLAN_phase0.md Q5). Every label below is the one label of its destination (board section F: 'State champions' not 'Champions', 'Contact' not 'Contact form' or 'Contact us', 'Scholastic' not 'Scholastic chess', 'Clubs' not 'Find a club' or 'Chess clubs', 'LCA on Facebook ↗' not 'Facebook ↗', 'Board & regions' not 'Board members', 'Website help' not 'Support'); the sheet's 'All tournaments' and 'All clubs' rows are built from the section's own label, not stored as a second one.

Shape. src/lib/nav.ts is pure and typed: no React, no router, no fetch, no import from domain/contracts or zod (test/unit/client-sections-audit.test.ts), no colour or class name. It imports FEATURES and the Features type from '@/lib/features', the role helpers it needs from '@/areas/admin/roles' (canAccessAdmin, isViewOnlyAdmin, WORKSPACE_ROLES and the MemberRole type, so no second definition of those rules exists) and, for the region aliases, REGIONS from '@/lib/regions' (which re-exports @domain/clubs/regions). Everything that depends on a switch takes a Features-shaped argument that defaults to FEATURES, so a test can try any combination without reloading modules. Icons are names in a string union (for example 'trophy', 'users', 'user' and 'menu', all of which exist in the installed lucide-react), not components, so the model stays node-testable; the step that draws the tabs maps a name to its icon. The names below are suggestions; the record names the ones used.

One entry per destination, with its id, its one label, its address, whether it leaves the site (and whether it opens in a new tab), the switch that makes it live (none for a page that exists today), and a kind: a page; an action (Log in, Join LCA, Renew, Donate, Search, Log out); the Facebook page (leaves the site, opens in a new tab, address https://www.facebook.com/LouisianaChessAssociation as Navbar.tsx and Footer.tsx write it); the contact email (a mailto link to LouisianaChess@gmail.com, which src/pages/ContactPage.tsx line 12 holds as LCA_EMAIL; it leaves the site's pages but not in a new tab). The entries:
- The six sections, in this order: Tournaments (/tournaments), Clubs (/clubs), Scholastic (/scholastic), News (/news), Membership (/membership) and About (the menu: it has no page of its own, its first row About LCA opens /about).
- Tournaments' children: 'Scoresheet scanner' (/scanner; today's header says 'Scanner'), 'This weekend' (/tournaments?when=weekend, live with newTournaments), 'Calendar' (/tournaments?view=calendar, live with newTournaments; footer Play column) and 'Results' (/results, live with newNews).

- About's rows in the menu's order: 'About LCA' (/about), 'Board & regions', 'Bylaws & rules', 'Minutes', 'Annual meeting' (/meeting), 'State champions', 'Contact' (/contact); then the footer row 'LCA on Facebook ↗'. Seven rows plus the footer row.
- The About rows' addresses by switch: Board & regions, Bylaws & rules and Minutes open /about/board, /about/bylaws and /about/minutes once newAbout is on, and /governance/board, /governance/bylaws and /governance/minutes until then; State champions opens /about/champions once newNews is on (whatever newAbout says) and /champions until then. The footer's and the trust line's links to the same destinations are the same entries by id, so they follow. /governance/rules is a redirect and is not a row.
- Donate: one entry, the About menu's last row above the Facebook row when the bar is squeezed, and the same entry in the header utilities, the sheet and the footer. Brief 1.4 gives it no address before WS12 builds /give: until newMembership is on it opens today's donation dialog (src/components/DonateButton.tsx, which no page imports yet), so the entry says it opens the dialog and has no address; with newMembership on it opens /give. This is the default of the plan's open question 1.
- Utilities and account: 'Search' (/search, live with siteSearch), 'Log in' (/login), 'Join LCA' (/membership), 'Renew' (/membership), 'My LCA' (/dashboard), 'Family' (/dashboard, today; WS13 moves it), 'Membership card' (live with newMembership; brief 1.4 gives no address, so choose one, for example /dashboard/you, where WS13 puts the card, and record it), 'Workspace' (/workspace), 'Admin' and 'Admin (view only)' (/admin), 'Board inbox' (/board/inbox), 'My region’s clubs' (/dashboard; written with the typographic apostrophe, exactly as Navbar.tsx line 80 writes it, so a browser spec can match today's link) and 'Log out' (an action). 'Membership help' (/contact?subject=membership) and 'Website help' (/support) are footer and sheet entries.
- The search pages: every entry that is a page, which is the 'about 40 static entries from nav.ts' of Q5; do not pin a count.

Sections and the routes each owns, for aria-current and the sheet's 'You are here' (a function of the pathname, using the rule today's header uses: the path equals the prefix or starts with it plus '/'): Tournaments owns /tournaments, /scanner and /results; Clubs owns /clubs; Scholastic owns /scholastic; News owns /news; Membership owns /membership, /donate and /give (with their /success and /thanks children); About owns /about, /governance, /champions, /state-champions, /meeting and /contact. /support, /search, /login, /dashboard and the rest belong to no section. The four tabs, with icons: the first two are the Tournaments and Clubs entries themselves (the first reads 'Tournaments'); the third is Log in when signed out and My LCA when signed in; the fourth is 'Menu' (reads 'Close' while the sheet is open). A function says which tab is current for a pathname: Tournaments and Clubs for their sections, the third for /login and /dashboard, and Menu for Scholastic, News, Membership and About (board section A, note 7).

The phase 0 replan also lists a synonym group (rating, the old initials for US Chess, and ID) pointing to a page called 'US Chess ID help'; no such page exists, so leave the group out and list it as a follow-up. The record never writes the old initials; the table holds no old initials either. K reviews the synonym list once (Q5).

The My LCA rows, as a pure function of what the person holds. Input (plain data, so the function needs no React): the role (MemberRole), isBoardMember (the context computes it from seats, so pass it in rather than recompute it), the number of managed clubs, the number of events directed, whether the person has children (hasChildren: AuthContext keeps member, seats, managedClubs and directedTournaments; GET /api/me also returns children and registrations, but the context drops them, so step 17 wires hasChildren; this slice's function takes the boolean) and the Features. Output: ordered rows with an id, a label, an address (none for an action), and whether it is a role row. The order, which AC17 sets and which wins over the board where they differ: My LCA; Family (only for a parent or guardian); Membership card (only while newMembership is on); today's role rows (only while myLcaRail is off), in this order: Workspace, Board inbox, My region’s clubs; the Admin row the person holds; Log out. The role rows are exactly what useAccountLinks gives today, minus Admin: Workspace when !canAccessAdmin(role) and (WORKSPACE_ROLES includes the role or the person directs an event); Board inbox when isBoardMember; My region’s clubs when role !== 'lca_admin' and the person has managed clubs. The Admin row is 'Admin' for lca_admin and 'Admin (view only)' for lca_officer and lca_observer (OBSERVER_ROLES, isViewOnlyAdmin), with no count (open question 5, step 17 of the plan keeps it so until WS08). With myLcaRail on, no person, a club rep included, gets a Workspace, Board inbox or My region row, and the word Workspace is in no row, title or label of the model.
